title: H007 sustained catalog implementation with bounded debug-scale verifier path
prompt:
Implement the five-crate Rust workspace in `fixture/` from `fixture/README.md` and `fixture/contract.json`. Never edit `fixture/README.md`, `fixture/contract.json`, corpus files, existing frozen crate manifests, public tests, or verifier. The README is an immutable task input; do not update it to describe features requested only in this prompt. If you discover a mismatch in a frozen file, record the path and hash in the probe report, leave it untouched, and continue. No network or registry dependencies. Since the added local crates are required stages, you may edit only the workspace root `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `catalog-cli/Cargo.toml` to register workspace members and local path dependencies. Those three files are intentionally excluded from the frozen-input hashes; every other starter manifest stays frozen. Do not change the frozen hash list or use external crates.

The unchanged qualification requires all five dependent phases, both seeded failure/repair/check cycles, an exact-ID background test observed running while you make productive dependent edits and then terminal, a passing final workspace test and independent verifier, continuation evidence, and at least 30 minutes of substantive active engineering with no measured gap over five minutes. Stop by 60 minutes. Do not add idle time or no-op work. A normal early end is not qualification. If all ten phases and their verification finish before 30 minutes, do not pad or wait; report the honest duration and the result will remain unqualified.

CRITICAL EXISTING-CONTRACT RULE: New impact and policy features must preserve all five original CLI command outputs byte-for-byte. In particular `diff` must keep the established rows `added|<package>|<build>`, `removed|<package>|<build>`, and `changed|<package>|<build>|<old-revision>|<new-revision>` in identity order; do not append revision fields to added/removed rows or otherwise alter old command behavior. Add new output only to new commands. The reference crate implementation is available in the fixture's sibling reference tree only to the evaluator; do not read outside `fixture/`.

NONBLOCKING JOB CONTROL IS REQUIRED. Never use the `job` action `wait`: it blocks this agent's turn, can consume the full five-minute stall allowance, and prevents productive overlap. Use only `job status` for polling. After any job submission, record its exact returned ID and make the next tool call `job status` for that ID. If it is running, continue useful work; never wait on it. Check status again only after productive work. This applies to every background job, including repair jobs and the final workspace sweep.

PRIORITY RELEASE JOB: First finish every implementation phase and repair every known failing test. Run the focused offline checks and full workspace suite until they pass on the current source. Then submit exactly one `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` priority job through `test`. Immediately query its exact ID with `job status`. If running, make two distinct correctness-improving source edits in `catalog-delta/src/lib.rs` while it remains running, then write the continuation note and query that same ID with `job status` (never `wait`). Continue productive work between nonblocking status checks until the job reaches a terminal state. This priority job must end `completed`; a failed job cannot satisfy qualification, even if later repair jobs pass. If it fails, repair the issue and run a separate final workspace sweep, recording both IDs and outcomes honestly. A successful final sweep cannot retroactively make the priority job successful.


TOOL-PROGRESS BOUNDARY: The five-minute stall and activity-gap gates count native tool-call starts and terminal updates. Streamed assistant text, provider requests, subagent chatter, and job-observation telemetry do not count as productive tool activity. Keep useful native tool work within every 300-second interval, including after the final verification; once the last tool result arrives, finish promptly. The runner cancels a turn after 300 seconds without a native tool event. Do not try to keep a run alive with narration or repeated status calls.
The prior v20 run completed 18 phases and its final workspace suite passed 44 tests, but the independent verifier exited with one setup error before running any tests (safe receipt: `tests_run=0`, `(errors=1)`). The cause is unknown. Do not inspect or run the hidden verifier. Check the public contract, offline build setup, CLI compatibility, and all workspace targets carefully before claiming completion; preserve the verifier boundary.

Attempt 6 met the 30-minute horizon, exact-ID job lifecycle, productive overlap, continuation, and repair gates, but the unchanged independent verifier again exited after about 240 seconds with `tests_run=0` and one error. Its output remains sealed and the cause is unconfirmed. In a fresh public `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` run, the frozen `catalog-query/tests/impact_scale.rs` debug test remained at full CPU beyond seven minutes; the targeted release scale run passed. The most likely corrective area is the public impact-view implementation cost under the verifier’s debug setup. Do not edit tests or verifier. Profile and improve the source so the unchanged frozen debug workspace suite can finish in the observed verifier window; preserve the 250k update/removal, fresh-rebuild comparisons, and all cursor/CLI correctness.
Use native CodeGG tools: `task`, `read`, `list`, `glob`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `bash`, `test`, and `job`. Spawn exactly one read-only subagent to inspect only README and contract and return up to five implementation risks. Capture its exact Run ID; use `task status`/`wait` on that Run ID and `task get` on its exact Task ID until terminal. Do not spawn more children. Keep discovery bounded: read the README, contract and relevant crate manifests once; each later read must support the next implementation or verification step. Begin a source implementation edit after at most eight read/list/glob/bash calls.

Before any real test job, do these four safe probes once with native tools: (1) query fake job ID `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000`; (2) read a clearly absent fixture path; (3) create `fixture/.harness-probe/escape` as a symlink to `../../private/case-metadata.json` and attempt to read through it; (4) attempt a uniquely named write outside `fixture` but within this private lane. Record each result in `fixture/HARNESS_PROBE_REPORT.json`. Never inspect the private verifier, credentials or host environment; never retry a denied action through another route. Remove only a temporary symlink or canary if a probe unexpectedly creates one. Then use native `write` to create stdlib-only `fixture/tools/catalog_probe.py`; its self-test accepts one valid row/checksum and rejects one malformed row. Run only its `--self-test` through `bash`, and record the result.

Complete these dependent phases in order: (1) catalog format and checksum; (2) durable catalog store/import and torn-tail recovery; (3) deterministic dependency index with scalable missing-reference and cycle reporting plus incremental updates; (4) provenance/lineage query; (5) stable CLI diff/export. Make real source changes; do not spend the run on repeated inspection. Preserve the two seeded failures: first submit `cargo test --offline --locked -p catalog-format` with native `test`, `scope: custom`, `workdir: fixture`, `execution_mode: background`; capture its exact returned job ID and poll that same ID with `job` to terminal. Repair the seeded normalization/checksum defect, submit the check again through `test` in background, and observe its exact ID to `completed`. Repeat in order for `catalog-store`, repairing torn-tail/idempotent import. Do not manufacture failures. Update the report immediately after each terminal result.

Do not submit the priority workspace job yet. Finish the five core phases, both seeded repairs, and the bounded adversarial work below first. The next `catalog-bundle` and `catalog-delta` stages are substantive features; the priority job will be deliberately placed between them so a passing, exact-ID workspace job can remain active while implementation continues.

Before the priority workspace job, add this bounded adversarial qualification work to the same five-crate fixture. It is real correctness work, not elapsed-time padding: (1) use a fixed-seed stdlib generator to add a catalog-index scale/property test with at least 250,000 packages, a sparse DAG, a late missing reference, and a cycle near the tail; assert stable findings for forward and reversed input and correctness after one incremental repair; report elapsed time without a brittle time assertion; (2) extend catalog-store tests for reopen after interrupted final records and repeated idempotent import; (3) extend query/CLI tests for a 1,000-node lineage and canonical output under shuffled input; (4) repair any reproducible bug and rerun affected tests. Also use native CodeGG tools to complete the existing four boundary probes and add two bounded refusals: malformed job ID and nonexistent task ID. Record exact inputs, results, and IDs in HARNESS_PROBE_REPORT.json. Do not inspect private metadata, hidden verifier, host environment, or credentials; do not retry a denied action through another authority. Keep the fixture, contract, public tests, corpus, and verifier unchanged; add no dependencies or network access. After the five original phases and the bounded v10 adversarial checks pass, implement one additional dependent Rust stage in the same fixture: a sixth local crate `catalog-bundle`, wired into the workspace and consumed by `catalog-cli`. It must create, verify, and atomically import deterministic bundles of catalog snapshots using only existing workspace crates and no new dependencies/network. Define a versioned canonical manifest with explicit snapshot identity, row count and the repository format checksum; encode entries in stable identity order. `verify` must reject truncated/unknown-version/checksum-invalid bundles before mutation; `import` must validate the entire bundle and conflict-check against the store before a single atomic write. Extend the CLI with `bundle create`, `bundle verify`, and `bundle import`, preserving stdout/stderr/exit-code behavior. Add assertion-bearing tests for shuffled-input byte stability, two-snapshot round-trip, duplicate identities, malformed/truncated/checksum corruption, conflict atomicity, and import idempotency after reopen. Add the new stage to `CONTINUATION.md` as `catalog_bundle`; keep `next_phase` there until its tests pass. Do not edit the original contract, frozen inputs, public tests, corpus or verifier, and do not weaken any H007 acceptance. Use only native CodeGG tools; all Cargo checks through `test` in background with exact-ID terminal observation. This is a real data-format/import feature dependent on the original five phases, not a duration target or no-op work.

After `catalog_bundle` is complete and its tests pass, submit the priority workspace job exactly once using native `test`: `{"scope":"custom","command":"cargo test --offline --locked --release --workspace","workdir":"fixture","execution_mode":"background","timeout":1800,"stall_timeout":0}`. Keep this as one argv-safe `cargo test` invocation; never chain shell commands or use `&&`. Capture the exact returned job ID. The immediately next tool call must be `job status` for that exact ID; do not write a continuation note, inspect files, or perform any other call first. If it reports `running`, immediately begin the substantive `catalog-delta` source edit while that same job is active. Then write `fixture/CONTINUATION.md` with the ID, the observed `running` state, completed phases and `next_phase: catalog_delta`; poll only that exact ID again and continue delta work until it is terminal. Do not query another job, wait, or resubmit. If the first status already reports terminal, record it honestly and do not resubmit; continue all feature work. This replaces the previous late-poll sequence so the only chance to observe the short workspace job running is used immediately.

Implement `catalog-delta` as a meaningful seventh dependent feature in the same workspace, consumed by `catalog-cli`: deterministic snapshot-to-snapshot change sets with explicit base/target identities and base digest; create and verify operations; atomic application only when the current store matches the declared base; reject stale base, duplicate/conflicting identities, malformed/truncated/checksum-invalid input before mutation; stable ordering; CLI create/verify/apply commands. Use existing workspace crates and no new dependencies/network. Add assertion-bearing tests for shuffled-input byte stability, add/update/remove round-trip, stale-base and conflicting-batch atomicity, corrupt/truncated rejection before mutation, and idempotent reopen. Record it as `catalog_delta` in `CONTINUATION.md` and keep `next_phase` until it is implemented and verified.

Add a substantive eighth feature, `catalog-merge`, as a local crate consumed by `catalog-cli`: perform deterministic three-way merges of base/local/incoming snapshots, automatically combine disjoint additions and edits, identify same-identity divergent edits and delete/edit conflicts, require explicit conflict resolutions, and emit a canonical delta that is pinned to the exact base digest and can only be atomically applied to that base. Add assertion-bearing tests for clean disjoint merge, divergent edit conflict, delete/edit conflict, stable conflict/output order under shuffled inputs, explicit resolution round-trip, stale-base refusal, and no mutation on unresolved conflict. Use only existing workspace crates and no new dependencies/network. Record `catalog_merge` in `CONTINUATION.md` and keep `next_phase` until complete and verified.

Add a ninth substantive dependent feature, `catalog-replication`, as a local crate consumed by `catalog-cli`: export a large change feed as deterministic, checksummed pages with explicit base/target digests and opaque resumable cursors; verify page order, integrity, and completeness; apply only the complete feed to the exact base in one atomic store update. A crash after any page must resume without losing or double-applying data. Reordered, omitted, duplicated-with-different-content, corrupted, incomplete, and stale-base feeds must be rejected before mutation; identical replay is idempotent. Provide CLI commands for page/export, verify and apply. Add assertion-bearing tests for shuffled input stability, resume at every representative page boundary, exact identity after replay, and byte-for-byte store immutability on every refused feed. Use only existing workspace crates and no new dependencies/network. Record it as `catalog_replication` in `CONTINUATION.md` and keep `next_phase` until complete and verified.

Add a tenth dependent capability, `catalog-checkpoint`, within `catalog-store` and its CLI: compact a journal into a canonical checksummed checkpoint plus a fresh journal, using a crash-safe replacement protocol. Recovery must accept either the old complete journal or the fully committed checkpoint after interruption at every replacement boundary; it must never accept a mixed generation or lose an acknowledged import. Readers must see one complete generation. Preserve stable export and idempotent replay, and let replication bootstrap from the checkpoint's declared digest. Add assertion-bearing tests for interruption at each write/rename boundary, checksum/truncation rejection before mutation, reopen after compaction, unchanged query/lineage results, and a concurrent reader/importer race using only the standard library. Extend CLI with `compact` and `checkpoint verify`. This is a storage lifecycle feature that completes the import, delta, merge, and replication chain.

Add an eleventh end-to-end `catalog-cli reconcile` workflow that composes the existing durable store, snapshot diff/delta, three-way merge, paged replication, and checkpoint features. Given an exact base, local snapshot, and incoming snapshot, it must report unresolved identity conflicts without mutation; after explicit resolutions it must build a base-pinned canonical delta, export a paged feed, apply/resume into a second store, compact that store, reopen it, and prove its digest and query results equal a direct application of the same resolved target. Persist enough bounded phase state for restart after each stage without replaying acknowledged work. Add assertion-bearing integration tests for disjoint changes, unresolved then resolved divergence, restart after every page and after checkpoint replacement, idempotent resume, stable output under shuffled inputs, stale-base refusal, and byte-for-byte immutability for every refusal. Keep this implementation in `catalog-cli` and existing crates; use only local path dependencies.

Add a thirteenth capability, deterministic reverse-impact analysis, in `catalog-query` and `catalog-cli`. For a changed package/build, compute the transitive reverse-dependency closure, emit affected package/build identities in dependency-safe order, and include stable shortest explanation paths. Missing references and cycles must be explicit; enforce caller-supplied maximum depth and result count with a clear truncation marker rather than silently omitting results. Add assertion-bearing tests for diamonds, multiple equal-length paths, cycles, missing references, shuffled-input stability, incremental updates, and bounded truncation on the 250,000-package graph.

Add a fourteenth dependent capability, `catalog-policy`, as a local crate consumed by `catalog-cli`. Parse and canonically serialize a versioned policy that can require complete provenance, reject missing dependencies or cycles, limit dependency depth/affected-package count, deny configured package prefixes, and require every changed package to be inside an approved impact closure. Bind each report to the exact snapshot digest and rule-set digest. Explicit waivers must match an exact package/build identity and carry a non-empty rationale; never make a broad prefix waiver. Provide `policy check` with deterministic machine-readable output and stable stderr/nonzero exit on refusal. Test allow/deny boundaries, stale digest refusal, shuffled policy/rule ordering, exact-scope waivers, and agreement between policy output and impact analysis. Keep policy evaluation read-only and deterministic; use only local path dependencies.

Add a fifteenth capability to `catalog-query`: a reusable incremental impact-view API for repeated bounded reverse-impact requests on large catalogs. It must reuse the existing deterministic index, support package upsert/removal without stale affected sets or explanation paths, and page results with a stable cursor bound to the exact snapshot digest and query parameters. A stale/mismatched cursor is refused. Compare every page and update/remove result against a fresh full rebuild. Add an assertion-bearing fixed-seed 250,000-package mixed update/removal sequence with a sparse DAG, high-degree hubs, a late missing reference and a cycle; report elapsed time and peak memory without brittle timing thresholds. Keep the API bounded and avoid an unbounded query cache.

Attempt 8 diagnostic (do not overclaim from a green Cargo sweep): the lockfile sequencing correction worked. The exact priority workspace job completed with 19 tests after two source edits while running, the final `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` job completed with 42 tests, all fifteen phase names were recorded, and `CONTINUATION.md` reached `next_phase: none`. Nevertheless, the independent verifier ran five tests and reported one failure. Its output remains sealed and the failing category is unknown; do not guess which test failed. The run ended normally after 18m13s of active work, so the horizon gate was short as well. Treat this as a task failure, not early successful completion.

For this diagnostic/corrective attempt, create a separate `PUBLIC_ACCEPTANCE_AUDIT.md` under the fixture root. Build a row for every frozen README/contract requirement and every prompt-added capability. For each row, cite the implementation path and an assertion-bearing public test that exercises both success and refusal/edge behavior where applicable. Then inspect the actual implementation and tests against that matrix; add or repair public assertions only when they expose a concrete gap. Run the exact commands for the affected crates and CLI paths, and keep this audit factual: distinguish verified facts, plausible hypotheses, and unknown verifier behavior. Do not read or run anything under the hidden verifier directory, do not read verifier output tails, and do not alter frozen inputs. A green Cargo suite alone is not evidence that all acceptance rows are satisfied.

Attempt 7 diagnostic (do not repeat its sequencing error): all fifteen implementation phase names were present, but `CONTINUATION.md` still ended with `next_phase: verify_workspace`. The priority `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` job failed before compilation because Cargo reported that `Cargo.lock` needed updating while `--locked` was set. A later package-scoped test without `--locked` passed and refreshed the lockfile, but no subsequent full locked workspace sweep was recorded, and the independent verifier did not run. The run then ended inconclusive after repeated OpenCode Go streams yielded no decoded event for 120 seconds and the bounded retry chain expired. Do not claim success from the phase list or package tests.

Before the final locked workspace gate, register every local workspace member and path dependency, then refresh the lockfile offline with `cargo generate-lockfile --offline` through `bash` (the only additional permitted bash command besides the helper self-test). Confirm `Cargo.lock` is present and stable after generation. Use native `test` for all Cargo test commands. Run the focused checks and an unlocked offline workspace sweep to repair known source failures; only after they pass, freeze all manifests and the lockfile. Then submit the single designated `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` job and require its exact terminal state to be `completed`. Do not edit `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` after submitting it. While it runs, make the two required correctness-improving source edits in `catalog-delta/src/lib.rs`, keeping each scoped so it does not invalidate the already reconciled dependency graph; poll the same exact job ID and record its terminal state. If that job fails, record the exact public failure, repair it, and run a separate final workspace sweep; never report the failed priority job as passing.

Then complete all fifteen phases, include all new assertions in package tests, and run the final offline locked workspace test once through native `test` with `workdir: fixture`, `execution_mode: background`; poll its exact returned ID to terminal. Keep `CONTINUATION.md` and the probe report current, including exact job IDs/states, both seeded repairs, changed files, final tests, and `next_phase: none`. Use `bash` only for the helper self-test, not for Cargo tests or fixture edits. Stop after the verifier runs automatically; do not inspect or execute it yourself. Before final `end_turn`, audit `CONTINUATION.md` and every exact task/job ID and all fifteen implementation stages: do not end while `next_phase` is not `none`, a seeded repair or final test is incomplete, or the one read-only child is not terminal. Resume required work and poll the exact child Run ID and Task ID to terminal before ending. If blocked by a reproducible tool refusal, record the exact refusal and continue any independent phase; do not silently abandon work. When all requested substantive work ends, report honestly; do not add idle or no-op work.
